extracted.intended_audience: Peer reviewers of EPSRC funding proposals using the Je-S system
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers completing EPSRC peer review reports via the Joint Electronic Submission (Je-S) system, covering assessment criteria, expected conduct, timescales and how to submit reviews. Includes both what to evaluate in proposals and how to prepare and submit review reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality is one of the four core assessment criteria and 'remains the pre-eminent assessment criterion for all proposals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the scientific/technical quality of the proposed work; consider methodological rigor, soundness of approach and feasibility. Refer to scheme-specific guidance where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance is one of the four core assessment criteria and 'also plays a major role in the assessment process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing Importance, reviewers are asked to comment explicitly on the strategic fit of the proposal with respect to the portfolio EPSRC is trying to create. This should include comment on how the proposed research relates to EPSRC research areas and any strategic actions highlighted in them, and on where a successful research programme would position the UK in the global research landscape, identifying the international leaders in the area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: applicant and partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant and partnerships is one of the four core assessment criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the track record, expertise and suitability of the applicant(s) and the strength, relevance and value of any partnerships or collaborators. Consider whether the team has the skills and partnerships needed to deliver the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: resources and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and management is one of the four core assessment criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the requested resources are appropriate and justified, and whether the project management and institutional environment are likely to support successful delivery. Consider value for money and practicality of the management plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme-specific criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Some schemes may have additional scheme-specific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always refer to the specific call guidance and any scheme-specific instructions when reviewing a proposal, as they may add or change assessment expectations beyond the four core criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good reviewing practice
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximise their value, reviewer reports should aim to: provide clear and concise comments and recommendations; clearly identify strengths and weaknesses; give justification for overall markings; raise concerns in the form of questions for the applicant; provide constructive criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bear in mind how your report will be used: it will be fed back anonymously to the applicant (who may respond to factual inaccuracies or questions), and prioritisation panels will use reports as the chief tool for distinguishing between proposals. Provide evidence-backed judgements and actionable points for applicants and panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct: timely, objective, fair and informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments should be timely, objective, fair and informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot comment within the indicated timescale, confirm this immediately so an alternative reviewer can be approached or a deadline extended. If you do not feel qualified to comment at all, inform EPSRC immediately. Maintain objectivity and fairness; base judgements on evidence and relevant expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timescales and confidentiality of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on deadlines and confidentiality: confirm inability to meet deadlines or lack of qualification promptly; the assessment procedure can only accommodate confidential comments withheld from applicants in exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly about availability/competence. Do not assume confidentiality of comments—only use confidential/comments-to-assessors options in exceptional cases and follow any provided guidance on what may legitimately be withheld from applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit reviews (Je-S requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviews requested by EPSRC must be completed through the research councils’ Je-S system using tailored reviewer forms; PDF/downloadable versions of forms and guidance are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the electronic forms in Je-S to submit your review. If you prefer to work offline, download the PDF forms, complete them and then submit by cutting and pasting into the relevant Je-S sections. Refer to the Reviewer forms and guidance notes page before completing the Je-S form.
